question.text: A process has <math><mi>Δ</mi><mi>H</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>200</mn><mtext> </mtext><mi>J</mi><mtext> </mtext><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><msup><mrow><mi>l</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> and <math><mi>Δ</mi><mi>S</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>40</mn><mtext> </mtext><mi>J</mi><msup><mrow><mi>K</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><msup><mrow><mi>l</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>.</mo></math> Out of the values given below choose the minimum temperature above which the process will be spontaneous:

solution.text:
∆G=∆H-T∆S ....... (Gibbs Helmholtz Equation)

For a reaction to be spontaneous, ∆G<0

So, ∆H-T∆S<0

∆H<T∆S

∆H∆S<T

i.e. Minimum temp. should be ⇒∆H∆S=20040=5K
